object_description: three independent buildings arranged around a common square
design_condition: The three buildings are arranged around a common square facing the main course, improving western accessibility but placing a long school bar in front of the existing courtyard and obstructing distant views.

positive.statement: The decision to separate the main functions into three houses is appreciated.

position.rationale: The plan clearly shows three independent masses arranged as a clustered group.

positive.statement: The system allows users to experience the school as a campus with distinct locations for the main activities.

position.rationale: Separate buildings and intervening open space visibly produce a campus-like spatial arrangement.

positive.statement: The four interior courtyards provide overhead light and breathing space for students.

position.rationale: Interior courtyards are not distinctly resolved, so the large southern-right building provides an approximate anchor.

positive.statement: The expression of the buildings is convincing and gives the project an institutional character.

position.rationale: Distinct elevation bands across the separated buildings support an institutional facade reading.

positive.statement: The facades present nuances specific to each activity without affecting the overall reading.

position.rationale: Separate masses permit approximate facade anchors, though activity-specific treatments are not distinguishable.

negative.statement: The long school bar in front of the existing courtyard is regrettable.

position.rationale: The elongated northern bar is clearly visible and stands in front of the other plan elements.

negative.statement: The entrance porticos of the two other houses seem narrow.

position.rationale: Porticos are not distinguishable; the western southern house is used as an approximate entrance anchor.

negative.statement: The sports house raises questions because of its ungenerous entrance space and changing rooms spread over four floors.

position.target: sports house entrance space and changing rooms
position.rationale: The smaller western house is a plausible sports-house anchor, while internal stacking is not represented.

negative.statement: The presence of classrooms on the ground floor was questioned.

position.rationale: Ground-level classrooms are not visible internally; the southern-right building surface supplies a constrained anchor.

negative.statement: The strong presence of the learning house closes the perspective from the existing courtyard towards the distant landscape.

position.rationale: The northern bar occupies the likely view corridor beyond the central open area.
